title: Detection of Rare Alleles in Bulk Seed Samples
author: Anthony Brusa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.brtam6ie
materials: Disrupt seeds using Qiagen Tissuelyser II (or similar equipment). Recommend grinding at 30hz in 90 second intervals. Visually inspect tube after each interval to determine if further grinding is needed. Ensure that all seeds have been properly disrupted. Depending on seed size this may take upwards of 6 minutes total grinding time.
Create 10nmol solutions of your KASP primers. (There will be three total. Two forward primers and one reverse)
Data interpretation Note: Standard software on lightcyclers is not designed for rare allele calling. Use the following steps instead.

steps.title: Assemble and Partition Seed Samples
steps.instruction: Assemble samples to be tested and partition them into pools of an appropriate number of seeds (e.g., 200 seeds for Amaranthus sp. testing).

steps.title: Prepare Seeds for Disruption
steps.instruction: Place seeds and a grinding bead into a tube suitable for tissue disruption, avoiding conical bottom tubes to ensure complete disruption.

steps.title: Lysis and Incubation
steps.instruction: Add 1mL lysis buffer (composed of 800 μL CLS-VF and 200 μL PPS in MPBio kit) to the tube, ensuring all seeds are submerged, and incubate overnight to soften the seed coat.

steps.title: Extract DNA
steps.instruction: Perform the remainder of the DNA extraction using the instructions from the kit or protocol of your choice.

steps.title: Prepare Primer Mix
steps.instruction: Create 150 µL of primer mix by combining the following components:

substeps.instruction: 3 µL of 10 µM forward primer (not A. palmeri)
20 µL of 10 µM forward primer (A. palmeri specific)

steps.title: Prepare Final Reaction Solution
steps.instruction: Combine 432 µL of KASP 2x Mastermix with 12 µL of the prepared primer mix.

steps.title: Plate Reaction Solution
steps.instruction: Plate 4 µL of the final reaction solution into a standard 96-well PCR plate.

steps.title: Add DNA Samples and Controls
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL of DNA solution (approximately 10-20 ng/μL) to each well, including positive controls, negative controls, and No Template Controls (NTCs).

substeps.instruction: Run 8 negative controls to assist in data interpretation.

steps.title: Run RT-PCR Program
steps.instruction: Run the samples on a Lightcycler or RT-PCR machine using the following thermal profile:

substeps.instruction: Touchdown program (9 cycles): 20 sec @ 94 °C, 60 sec @ 61 °C to 55 °C (incrementing with each cycle)
Endpoint fluorescence read: 30 seconds @ 28 °C at 465-510nm (FAM) and 533-580nm (HEX)

steps.title: Export and Import Data
steps.instruction: Export the raw 465-510nm and 533-580nm reads from the Lightcycler software as a .csv file and import them into statistical software (e.g., R, SPSS, SAS, Mathematica).

steps.title: Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Process the exported data to determine the presence of A. palmeri seeds.

substeps.instruction: Perform an arctan transform on the ratio of 465-510nm to 533-580nm reads to convert Cartesian coordinates into datapoint trajectories.
Generate a box-and-whisker plot using the software.
Perform a statistical comparison between the negative control and test samples.
